question: For the already selected densitized V=0 multiplication operator H_hat on the full real-p auxiliary spectral space, does the regular-shell RAQ test space complete to two independent L2(R,dx) branches with no origin atom inherited from the auxiliary spectral measure?

upstream_results.role: fixes the selected H_hat spectral multiplier and positive-branch interior shell measure
fixes the logarithmic nonzero-edge obstruction and forbids treating a finite part as an automatically selected origin sector

primary_sources.source: Marolf, Refined Algebraic Quantization: Systems with a Single Constraint, arXiv:gr-qc/9508015v3
primary_sources.used_for: single-constraint rigging-map and distributional zero-fiber framework
primary_sources.not_used_for: selecting this repository's p=0 origin sector, branch gluing, or raw-C realization

primary_sources.source: Han and Thiemann, Rigging Inner Product and Master Constraint Direct Integral Decomposition, arXiv:0911.3431v1
primary_sources.used_for: the conditional direct-integral comparison and the need to state the regularity and test-space hypotheses
primary_sources.not_used_for: proving raw-C versus densitized-H equivalence or making a measure-zero fiber canonical

primary_sources.source: Pawlowski and Ashtekar, Positive Cosmological Constant in Loop Quantum Cosmology, arXiv:1112.0360v1
primary_sources.used_for: a contrast case in which a genuine self-adjoint extension and gluing choice occurs
primary_sources.not_used_for: importing an LQC boundary condition into the selected multiplication operator

declared_model.operator: the maximal self-adjoint multiplication operator M_h
declared_model.origin_rule: no delta identity is applied at the critical origin and no origin-supported auxiliary atom or rigging functional is added

assumptions: hbar and r_star are strictly positive; numerical checks use hbar=1
the selected maximal multiplication operator and Lebesgue auxiliary measure are not changed
Phi_reg is dense in the auxiliary Hilbert space because the excluded axes and origin are auxiliary-measure null
the regular coarea formula is applied only for r>0 where the transverse derivative is nonzero
completion means the Hilbert completion of Phi_reg modulo the null space of the declared regular-shell positive form
adding an origin atom, logarithmic finite part, parity/CPT quotient, or cross-branch gluing would define extra data outside this calculation
tasks: derive the unique positive-kappa root and transverse coarea derivative on both p signs
derive the full regular-shell form as the orthogonal sum of the positive and negative rays
construct the normalized x=log(r/r_star) branch maps and verify their exact isometry
show that changing r_star is only a unitary translation of x
record the branch projectors, sign observable, parity exchange, and p multiplication action without imposing a quotient
show that the selected auxiliary spectral projection has no zero eigenprojection or independent origin atom
independently compare fixed regular witness norms in r and x coordinates at two reference scales
leave raw C, exact endpoint, absolute BFV, inhomogeneous, relational, empirical, physics and TOE outputs null

decision_table.condition: the executable root, coarea, disjoint-branch, normalized log-coordinate isometry, scale-translation and branch-operator checks plus all independent quadratures pass, while the density, trace-range and no-auxiliary-atom theorem hypotheses are explicitly scoped
any executable root, coarea, disjoint-branch, isometry, scale, branch-algebra, observable, or independent quadrature check fails

computed_scope: the regular zero shell of one selected full-real-p multiplication operator
the exact two-ray coarea form and normalized logarithmic coordinates
the regular-shell Hilbert completion and inherited multiplication observables
six bounded high-precision witness quadratures with no roots or ODEs
not_computed: an ordering, self-adjoint domain, extension, rigging map, or physical inner product for undensitized raw C
quantum equivalence between raw C, selected H, or the declared Mc representation
a canonical p=0 counterterm, finite part, origin-supported sector, boundary state, branch quotient, or CPT/parity gluing law
an exact endpoint transform, full symbol, restricted Mc target, or companion-observable intertwiner
a lapse contour, modulus, absolute BFV trajectory measure, determinant-line orientation, or gluing theorem
inhomogeneous constraints, S3 harmonic closure, operator anomaly, BRST cohomology, relational observables, semiclassical recovery, decoherence, likelihood, quantum gravity, physics, or TOE
